name: ZITLAS Baked Aloo Paratha
description: A classic potato-stuffed paratha, but roasted with a bare minimum of oil rather than the usual generous ghee — a genuinely lighter version of the most common Indian breakfast paratha.
instructions: Mash boiled potato with green chilli, coriander and ajwain.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the potato mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a hot tawa using only a light brushing of oil rather than pooling it.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Deliberately low-oil roasting technique keeps this meaningfully lighter than a typical restaurant aloo paratha
The most requested classic paratha, finally represented in the database
Filling, familiar comfort food

name: ZITLAS Gobi Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with finely grated cauliflower (gobi) — a distinct low-calorie vegetable filling from potato, peas or beetroot already used.
ingredients: Ginger, green chilli, garam masala — 5 g
instructions: Grate cauliflower finely, squeeze out excess water, and mix with ginger, green chilli and garam masala.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the cauliflower mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Cauliflower is a genuinely low-calorie, high-volume filling distinct from every other vegetable paratha in the database
Classic North Indian combination
Good weight-loss-friendly stuffed paratha option

name: ZITLAS Mooli Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with grated radish (mooli) — a peppery, high-water filling distinct from every other vegetable paratha in the database.
instructions: Grate radish finely, squeeze out excess water thoroughly (essential to avoid a soggy paratha), and mix with green chilli, coriander and ajwain.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the radish mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd and pickle.
why_it_works: Radish's sharp, peppery flavour is distinctly different from any other vegetable filling in the database
Traditional North Indian winter breakfast
Very low calorie filling

name: ZITLAS Thalipeeth
description: A Maharashtrian multi-flour savoury pancake made from a blend of jowar, bajra and besan — an entirely different cooking technique from any chilla, dosa or paratha, mixed and patted directly on the tawa.
instructions: Mix the three flours with onion, cumin seeds and ajwain, and enough water to form a soft, pliable dough.
Pat the dough directly onto a hot, lightly oiled tawa with wet hands into a thin round (a distinct technique from rolling with a pin).
Poke a few holes in the centre with a finger, drizzle a little oil, and cook covered until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Multi-flour blend gives a broader nutrient profile than any single-grain flatbread in the database
Hand-patted-on-the-tawa technique is genuinely different from rolling a dough with a pin
Traditional Maharashtrian breakfast staple

name: ZITLAS Sabudana Thalipeeth
description: A thalipeeth made primarily from crushed sabudana and boiled potato — a fasting-day-style flour-free version, distinct from the mixed-grain thalipeeth.
instructions: Mix soaked sabudana with mashed potato, crushed peanuts, green chilli and cumin seeds into a soft dough.
Pat directly onto a hot, lightly oiled tawa into a thin round.
Cook covered until golden on both sides, flipping once.
Serve hot with curd.
Note: sabudana needs overnight soaking, not counted in active prep time above.
why_it_works: Flour-free, fasting-day-appropriate ingredient base distinct from the grain-flour thalipeeth
Same hand-patting technique applied to a genuinely different base
Peanuts supply most of the protein here

name: ZITLAS Misal Pav Bowl
description: Sprouted moth bean curry topped with crunchy farsan and served with pav — a spicier, farsan-topped format distinct from the plain Matki Usal Bowl.
ingredients: Misal masala or goda masala — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook soft.
Add boiled matki and misal masala with water to form a thin, spicy gravy; simmer 10 minutes.
Ladle into a bowl and top with a handful of farsan (store-bought or homemade thin sev) just before serving.
Serve with pav on the side.
why_it_works: The farsan topping and pav pairing make this a genuinely different eating experience from the plain Matki Usal Bowl already in the database
Iconic Maharashtrian breakfast, distinctly spicier and more textured
Filling, complete meal-style breakfast

name: ZITLAS Dabeli
description: A Kutchi-style spiced mashed potato filling stuffed into a pav with peanuts, pomegranate and chutney — a distinctly sweet-tangy-spicy regional street food not resembling any other roll or sandwich in the database.
instructions: Mash boiled potato with dabeli masala and a spoon of tamarind chutney until well combined.
Warm the mixture in a pan with a little oil.
Slice the pav and lightly toast the cut sides.
Stuff with the spiced potato, then top with roasted peanuts and pomegranate seeds before closing.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: The sweet-tart-crunchy combination of tamarind chutney, peanuts and pomegranate makes this genuinely distinct from every other bun or roll in the database
Kutchi (Gujarat) street food rarely represented in fitness recipe collections
Peanuts and pomegranate turn a simple potato filling into something texturally complex

name: ZITLAS Baked Moong Dal Kachori
description: A whole wheat kachori filled with spiced moong dal, baked instead of deep-fried — a distinct pastry-like format not represented anywhere else in the database.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and coarsely ground — 70 g
instructions: Cook the ground moong dal with fennel seeds, ginger and asafoetida in a dry pan until thick and moisture-free; cool.
Knead atta with a little oil and water into a firm dough.
Roll small discs, stuff with the dal filling, seal and flatten gently.
Preheat oven to 200°C and bake the kachoris for 18-20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Baking instead of deep-frying keeps this meaningfully lighter than a traditional kachori while keeping the flaky, stuffed pastry format
A pastry-style stuffed bread not represented anywhere else in the database
Good make-ahead batch option

name: ZITLAS Baked Vegetable Samosa Bites
description: Small whole wheat samosas filled with spiced mixed vegetables, baked rather than fried — a bite-sized version distinct from the full-size kachori.
instructions: Cook finely chopped vegetables with cumin seeds and garam masala in a dry pan until soft and moisture-free.
Knead atta with a little oil and water into a firm dough.
Roll small discs, fold into cones, stuff with the vegetable filling and seal into small triangles.
Preheat oven to 200°C and bake for 18-20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Serve with tamarind chutney.
why_it_works: Bite-sized, baked format cuts the oil dramatically compared to deep-fried samosas while keeping the familiar shape and crunch
Vegetable-only filling distinct from the dal-filled kachori in this batch
Good for sharing or a family breakfast

name: ZITLAS Aloo Kulcha
description: A soft, curd-leavened kulcha stuffed with spiced potato — a different filling from the paneer kulcha already in the database, using the same distinct dough technique.
instructions: Knead maida with curd and water into a soft dough; rest 15 minutes.
Mash potato with onion, coriander and garam masala for the filling.
Roll out the dough, stuff with the potato filling and seal.
Roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden with brown spots on both sides.
Serve hot with pickle.
why_it_works: Same curd-leavened kulcha dough as the paneer version but with a distinctly different, more traditional filling
Soft, pillowy texture unlike a plain roti
Restaurant-style comfort food at home

name: ZITLAS Khaman
description: A fluffy, spongy steamed besan snack made with a different batter ratio and technique from dhokla, giving it a distinctly lighter, more porous texture.
instructions: Whisk besan with curd and water into a thin, well-beaten batter (beat vigorously for extra air, unlike a standard dhokla batter).
Add eno fruit salt and mix gently just before steaming.
Pour into a greased tin and steam for 12-15 minutes until well risen and spongy.
Cut into cubes, then temper mustard seeds and green chilli in oil and pour over the top.
why_it_works: Deliberately thinner batter and vigorous beating give khaman a distinctly spongier, lighter texture than the denser dhokla already in the database
Steamed, essentially fat-free base
Classic Gujarati street food

name: ZITLAS Rava Dhokla
description: A steamed dhokla made from semolina (rava) instead of besan — a different grain base with a distinctly grainier texture from the besan, oats, moong or multigrain versions.
instructions: Whisk rava with curd and water into a thick batter; rest 15 minutes to let the rava soften.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into a greased tin and steam for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil poured over the top.
why_it_works: Semolina base gives a distinctly grainier bite from the smoother besan or moong dhokla already in the database
Faster to prepare since rava needs no grinding
Steamed, low added fat

name: ZITLAS Instant Rava Dosa
description: A thin, lacy, crisp dosa made from a rava-rice flour batter that needs no fermentation — a distinctly different texture and technique from the fermented urad-rice dosas already in the database.
instructions: Whisk rava and rice flour with plenty of water into a thin, watery batter (much thinner than a regular dosa batter); rest 15 minutes.
Mix in onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Pour the batter from height around the edges of a hot tawa first, then fill the centre, to create lacy holes.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until crisp and golden; no flipping needed.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: No-fermentation, instant technique is genuinely different from every fermented dosa or idli batter in the database
Distinctly lacy, crisp texture unlike a soft, thick dosa
Good for when there's no time to plan a fermented batter ahead

name: ZITLAS Neer Dosa
description: An ultra-thin, soft rice dosa from Mangalore made without fermentation or urad dal — a distinctly different rice-only batter and delicate texture from any other dosa in the database.
instructions: Soak rice for at least 2 hours, then grind with water into a very thin, watery batter, thinner than any other dosa batter used elsewhere.
Heat a tawa, pour a thin layer of batter and swirl quickly to spread it thin.
Cover and cook briefly until the edges lift, without flipping.
Fold gently into a soft, delicate dosa.
Serve with coconut chutney or a light curry.
Note: rice needs 2+ hours soaking, folded into prep time above.
why_it_works: Rice-only, no-urad, no-fermentation batter is genuinely distinct from every other dosa technique in the database
Delicate, soft texture (not crisp) sets it apart from Instant Rava Dosa or a regular dosa
Coastal Karnataka home cooking rarely represented in fitness recipe collections

name: ZITLAS Appam with Coconut Milk
description: A Kerala fermented rice-and-coconut-milk pancake, cooked in a curved pan for soft, spongy centres and lacy, crisp edges — a bowl-shaped format entirely unlike a flat dosa or uttapam.
instructions: Soak rice for several hours, grind with a little of the coconut milk into a smooth batter, mix in yeast and a pinch of sugar, and let ferment overnight.
Just before cooking, thin the batter with the remaining coconut milk and water.
Heat a curved appam pan (or a small kadai), pour a ladle of batter and swirl quickly up the sides.
Cover and cook until the centre is soft and set and the edges are golden and lacy.
Serve as is or with a light vegetable stew.
Note: batter needs overnight fermentation, not counted in active prep time above.
why_it_works: The curved-pan technique produces a bowl shape with a distinct soft-centre, crisp-edge texture unlike any flat dosa or uttapam in the database
Coconut milk gives a naturally mild sweetness without added sugar
Classic Kerala breakfast staple, genuinely different from Tamil or Karnataka rice preparations already represented

name: ZITLAS Puttu
description: Steamed layers of rice flour and grated coconut, cooked in a cylindrical mould — a distinctly different steamed texture (crumbly, not smooth like idli) from anything else in the database.
instructions: Sprinkle water gradually over rice flour, rubbing it in with your fingers until it reaches a coarse, breadcrumb-like consistency (not a smooth batter).
Layer the moistened flour and grated coconut alternately into a puttu mould (or a tall steamer vessel with holes).
Steam for 10-12 minutes until firm.
Unmould onto a plate and serve with banana or a light curry on the side.
why_it_works: Layered, crumbly steamed texture is entirely unlike the smooth batter of an idli or the flat shape of a dosa
No fermentation and no blending required, just a coarse hand-mixed flour
Kerala breakfast staple rarely represented in fitness recipe collections

name: ZITLAS Adai
description: A thick, savoury dosa made from a coarse blend of rice and several dals together, needing no fermentation — a distinctly different batter composition and texture from any single-dal dosa in the database.
instructions: Soak rice and all three dals together for at least 4 hours, then grind coarsely (not smooth) with red chilli and ginger.
No fermentation needed — the batter can be used right after grinding.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread into a coarse, thick round.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until crisp on both sides.
Serve hot with jaggery and butter, or coconut chutney.
Note: soaking time folded into prep above.
why_it_works: Combining three dals with rice gives adai notably more protein and a coarser, heartier texture than any fermented dosa in the database
No fermentation wait needed, unlike a regular dosa
Traditional South Indian dish specifically designed around multi-pulse nutrition

name: ZITLAS Chettinad Egg Curry Bowl
description: Boiled eggs simmered in a fiery, freshly ground Chettinad-style spice paste — a distinctly different South Indian regional flavour profile from the Bengali or standard multigrain-roti egg curries in the database.
ingredients: Chettinad masala (fennel, star anise, dried chilli) — 6 g
instructions: Grind grated coconut with the Chettinad spice mix into a thick paste.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook soft.
Add the ground spice paste and a little water; simmer 8-10 minutes into a thick gravy.
Halve the boiled eggs and simmer in the gravy for 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot with rice or a plain dosa.
why_it_works: Chettinad spicing (fennel, star anise, coconut) is a genuinely distinct regional flavour direction from the Bengali panch-phoron or North Indian garam-masala egg curries already in the database
Freshly ground spice paste, not a pre-mixed masala powder
Tamil Nadu regional cuisine represented for the first time with eggs

name: ZITLAS Prawn Curry Rice Bowl
description: A light coconut-based prawn curry served over rice — introducing prawn, a seafood protein not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until soft, add turmeric and red chilli powder.
Add coconut milk and a little water, bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the prawns and cook for 4-5 minutes only, until just pink and cooked through (overcooking makes them rubbery).
Serve the curry over warm rice.
why_it_works: Prawns are a genuinely new protein source for the database, giving non-vegetarian users seafood variety beyond fish, chicken and mutton
Coconut-based gravy is light and quick to prepare
Prawns cook very fast, making this a realistically quick non-vegetarian breakfast

name: ZITLAS Lean Mutton Keema Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with spiced lean mutton mince — introducing mutton, a red meat protein not used anywhere else in the database, alongside the existing chicken keema paratha.
instructions: Cook the mutton mince with onion, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala in a pan until fully cooked and fairly dry; cool slightly.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the cooked mince filling and seal well.
Roll out carefully and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden and cooked through on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Mutton is a genuinely new red-meat protein source for the database, offering variety beyond chicken for non-vegetarian users
Lean mince selection keeps saturated fat more moderate than a fattier cut
Same proven stuffed-paratha technique as the chicken version, giving users a choice

name: ZITLAS Baked Kanda Bhaji Bites
description: Onion fritter batter shaped into small bites and baked instead of deep-fried — a lighter version of a popular tea-time snack, reframed for breakfast.
instructions: Mix thinly sliced onion with besan, rice flour, red chilli powder and turmeric, adding just enough water to bind (the onion releases its own moisture too).
Shape into small, loose bite-sized mounds on a lightly greased tray.
Bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Baking instead of deep-frying keeps the fat dramatically lower than a traditional kanda bhaji while keeping the crisp edges
Turns a popular monsoon tea-time snack into a genuinely lighter breakfast bite
Simple, mostly hands-off baking

name: ZITLAS Methi Thepla
description: A Gujarati flatbread made with fresh fenugreek leaves worked directly into the dough — a distinct bread-making tradition (thepla) from the paneer-stuffed Methi Paneer Paratha already in the database.
instructions: Knead atta and besan with chopped methi leaves, turmeric, ajwain and a little oil and water into a firm dough.
Roll out thin (theplas are rolled thinner than a regular roti) and roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden with brown spots.
Serve hot, often with curd or pickle.
why_it_works: Methi is kneaded directly into the dough itself, unlike the paneer version which uses methi only as a stuffing — a genuinely different construction technique
Theplas are traditionally rolled thinner and travel well, unlike a thicker paratha
Classic Gujarati travel-food staple

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Khichu
description: A steamed, spoonable rice-flour dumpling mixture flavoured with moong dal — a Gujarati steamed-batter format entirely unlike a chilla, dhokla or idli.
ingredients: Moong dal, cooked and mashed — 40 g
instructions: Bring water to a boil with cumin seeds and ajwain.
Slowly whisk in rice flour and mashed moong dal, stirring continuously to avoid lumps, until it thickens into a soft, cohesive dough-like mass directly in the pan.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with a little warm oil, and eat with a spoon.
why_it_works: Cooked and eaten with a spoon straight from the pan, unlike any steamed or pan-cooked dish elsewhere in the database
Moong dal addition raises protein above a plain rice-flour khichu
Simple, single-pot Gujarati home food

name: ZITLAS Egg Appam Bowl
description: Soft, spongy appam torn into pieces and served with a light egg curry — a distinct pairing from the classic coconut-stew accompaniment.
instructions: Ferment the rice-coconut milk batter overnight as for a regular appam.
Cook appams in a curved pan as usual.
Separately, saute onion in oil, add a little water and simmer the halved boiled eggs in a light gravy for 3-4 minutes.
Serve the appams with the egg curry spooned over or alongside.
Note: batter needs overnight fermentation, not counted in active prep time above.
why_it_works: Egg curry pairing raises the protein of a meal that's traditionally quite light on protein
Distinct from the standard vegetable stew accompaniment to appam
Genuinely different from any other egg preparation by the appam's soft, spongy texture

name: ZITLAS Baked Mathri Bites
description: Small, flaky whole wheat crackers, baked instead of deep-fried — a crunchy, shelf-stable snack reframed as a grab-and-go breakfast.
instructions: Knead atta with oil, ajwain, cumin seeds and just enough water into a firm, slightly stiff dough.
Roll out thick and cut into small discs, pricking each with a fork.
Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until firm and lightly golden.
Cool completely — mathri crisps up further as it cools.
Store in an airtight container for up to two weeks.
why_it_works: Baking removes almost all the oil a deep-fried mathri would need while keeping the flaky crunch
Long shelf life makes this a genuine grab-and-go option for busy mornings, unlike most other recipes here
Simple ingredient list, easy to batch

name: ZITLAS Puffed Rice Upma
description: A dry, tempered upma made from puffed rice (murmura) instead of rava or poha — a different, lighter-textured upma from anything else labelled 'upma' in the database.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute onion until soft.
Add turmeric and the puffed rice, tossing on low heat for just 2-3 minutes (puffed rice needs far less cooking than rava or poha).
Serve immediately while still light and crisp.
why_it_works: Puffed rice cooks in a fraction of the time of rava or poha upma and stays airier rather than dense
Genuinely different texture (light, crunchy) from the rava or poha versions already in the database
Very quick, very low cost

name: ZITLAS Baked Paneer Kachori Bites
description: Small whole wheat kachoris filled with spiced paneer, baked rather than fried — a distinct filling from the moong dal kachori already in this batch.
instructions: Mix crumbled paneer with onion, coriander and garam masala for the filling.
Knead atta with a little oil and water into a firm dough.
Roll small discs, stuff with the paneer filling, seal and flatten gently.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Paneer filling gives a softer, creamier bite than the drier moong dal kachori filling
Baked rather than fried, keeping this meaningfully lighter than a traditional kachori
Good make-ahead batch option

name: ZITLAS Sprouted Ragi Dosa
description: A dosa batter made by grinding sprouted ragi rather than plain ragi flour — a distinct preparation that changes both nutrition and flavour from the plain Ragi Dosa already in the database.
instructions: Sprout ragi grains over 1-2 days ahead of time (rinse and drain twice daily until small shoots appear), then grind with rice flour and curd into a batter.
Rest 15 minutes.
Heat a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp, then flip briefly.
Serve hot with chutney.
Note: sprouting ragi takes 1-2 days ahead of cooking, not counted in prep time above.
why_it_works: Sprouting ragi before grinding meaningfully changes its nutrient availability and gives a noticeably different, slightly sweeter flavour from the plain-flour Ragi Dosa in the database
A genuinely different preparation process, not just a renamed dish
High fiber, naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Bajra Thalipeeth
description: A single-grain bajra thalipeeth — a simpler, more traditional version distinct from the multi-flour blend used in the standard Thalipeeth recipe.
instructions: Mix bajra flour with onion, cumin seeds, green chilli and enough water to form a soft dough.
Pat directly onto a hot, lightly oiled tawa into a thin round.
Poke a few holes, drizzle oil, and cook covered until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Single-grain version offers a purer bajra flavour and texture, distinct from the blended multi-flour thalipeeth
Same hand-patting technique, simpler ingredient list
Good winter-season breakfast, bajra being traditionally warming

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Adai
description: Adai batter with finely chopped vegetables mixed in before cooking — a vegetable-forward variant of the plain multi-dal Adai earlier in this batch.
instructions: Soak rice and dals together for at least 4 hours, then grind coarsely with red chilli and ginger.
Mix in finely chopped vegetables.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread into a coarse round.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until crisp on both sides.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Vegetables mixed directly into the batter make this genuinely different from the plain multi-dal adai, adding fiber and micronutrients
Same protein-dense multi-dal base, broader nutrient profile
No fermentation needed

name: ZITLAS Chicken Keema Kulcha
description: A curd-leavened kulcha stuffed with spiced chicken mince — a non-vegetarian kulcha filling distinct from the paneer or potato versions already in the database.
instructions: Cook the chicken mince with ginger-garlic paste and garam masala until fully cooked and fairly dry; cool.
Knead maida with curd and water into a soft dough; rest 15 minutes.
Roll out, stuff with the cooked mince and seal.
Roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden with brown spots on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Non-vegetarian option within the soft, curd-leavened kulcha format, distinct from the vegetarian paneer and aloo versions
Lean mince keeps this high protein without excess fat
Same proven dough technique, different filling entirely

name: ZITLAS Chana Dal Khaman
description: A khaman made from ground chana dal instead of besan — a chunkier, higher-fiber variation on the classic spongy Gujarati steamed snack.
ingredients: Chana dal, soaked and ground — 120 g
instructions: Soak chana dal for at least 4 hours, grind with curd into a thick batter.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into a greased tin and steam for 12-15 minutes until well risen.
Cut into cubes, then temper mustard seeds and green chilli in oil and pour over the top.
why_it_works: Chana dal gives notably more protein and fiber than the refined besan version, with a slightly coarser bite
Same spongy steaming technique, genuinely different base pulse
Steamed, low added fat

name: ZITLAS Multigrain Thalipeeth
description: A thalipeeth made from a blend of five flours (jowar, bajra, ragi, besan, rice) — the most grain-diverse flatbread in the database, distinct from the three-flour standard Thalipeeth.
ingredients: Multigrain flour blend (jowar, bajra, ragi, besan, rice) — 70 g
instructions: Mix the multigrain flour blend with onion, cumin seeds, ajwain and enough water to form a soft dough.
Pat directly onto a hot, lightly oiled tawa into a thin round.
Poke a few holes, drizzle oil, and cook covered until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Broadest grain blend of any thalipeeth in the database, spreading fiber and micronutrients across five sources rather than one to three
Same reliable hand-patting technique
Good grain-rotation option across the week

name: ZITLAS Roasted Poha Chivda
description: Dry roasted (not oil-tempered) poha tossed with peanuts and light spices — a genuinely different technique from the tempered kanda poha or oil-based chivda preparations elsewhere.
instructions: Dry-roast the thin poha in a wide kadai on low heat, stirring constantly, until crisp — this takes longer than tempering but uses no extra oil for the poha itself.
Separately, roast peanuts and curry leaves in a little oil with turmeric.
Toss the roasted poha with the peanut mixture.
Cool and store, or eat warm.
why_it_works: Dry-roasting the poha itself (rather than tempering it wet with oil and vegetables) is a genuinely different technique from every other poha preparation in the database
Can be stored for several days, unlike the fresh, wet kanda poha
Very low oil overall

name: ZITLAS Baked Vegetable Kachori
description: A whole wheat kachori filled with spiced mixed vegetables (not moong dal or paneer), baked — completing three distinct fillings for the baked-kachori format introduced in this batch.
instructions: Cook finely chopped vegetables with fennel seeds and coriander powder in a dry pan until soft and dry.
Knead atta with a little oil and water into a firm dough.
Roll small discs, stuff with the vegetable filling, seal and flatten gently.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Vegetable-only filling gives users a lower-protein, higher-fiber choice alongside the moong dal and paneer kachoris in this batch
Baked, not fried, keeping this meaningfully lighter
Good vegan option within the kachori family

name: ZITLAS Sabudana Khichu
description: A khichu made from sabudana instead of rice flour — a distinct fasting-day-style spoonable steamed-in-pan dish from the Moong Dal Khichu earlier in this batch.
instructions: Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and green chilli.
Add soaked sabudana, crushed peanuts and water, stirring continuously as it thickens and turns translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and eat with a spoon, while warm.
why_it_works: Sabudana's translucent, chewy texture is genuinely different from the smoother rice-moong khichu
Traditionally a fasting-day dish, reframed as a regular breakfast option
One-pot, minimal cleanup

name: ZITLAS Paneer Adai
description: Adai batter topped with crumbled paneer just before flipping — a protein-boosted adai variant distinct from the plain or vegetable versions.
instructions: Soak rice and dals for at least 4 hours, grind coarsely with red chilli and ginger.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread into a coarse round.
Scatter crumbled paneer over the top while the first side cooks, pressing gently so it sticks.
Drizzle oil around the edges, flip carefully, and cook until crisp.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Paneer topping raises the protein of an already high-protein multi-dal base even further
Distinct from the plain and vegetable adai variants by adding a dairy protein layer
Same reliable no-ferment technique

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Puttu Bowl
description: Steamed puttu crumbled into a bowl and tossed with a light vegetable stir-fry — a distinct serving format from the traditional cylindrical unmoulded puttu.
instructions: Prepare and steam puttu as usual with rice flour and grated coconut.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute vegetables 3-4 minutes.
Crumble the steamed puttu into the pan and toss gently with the vegetables.
Serve warm in a bowl.
why_it_works: Crumbled-and-tossed bowl format is a genuinely different eating experience from the traditional unmoulded cylinder served plain
Vegetables add fiber and micronutrients not present in the plain version
Same steaming technique, different finishing

name: ZITLAS Egg Puttu Bowl
description: Steamed puttu crumbled and tossed with scrambled egg — a protein-added variant of the puttu family, distinct from the vegetable or plain versions.
instructions: Prepare and steam puttu as usual with rice flour and grated coconut.
Heat oil, saute onion, then scramble in the beaten egg until just cooked.
Crumble the steamed puttu into the pan and toss gently with the scrambled egg.
Serve warm in a bowl.
why_it_works: Egg addition meaningfully raises the protein of the traditionally protein-light puttu
Distinct texture combination — crumbly rice-coconut with soft scrambled egg
Same steaming technique, third distinct finishing in this batch

name: ZITLAS Fish Moilee Rice Bowl
description: A Kerala-style mild coconut-milk fish curry with curry leaves and turmeric, served over rice — a distinct regional fish preparation from the Bengali mustard-based fish curry already in the database.
ingredients: Curry leaves, turmeric, green chilli — 4 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute sliced onion until soft, add curry leaves, turmeric and green chilli.
Add coconut milk and a little water, bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish and simmer for 6-8 minutes until just cooked through, without stirring too much so it doesn't break apart.
Serve the curry over warm rice.
why_it_works: Coconut milk and curry leaves give a distinctly mild, creamy Kerala flavour profile, genuinely different from the mustard-and-panch-phoron Bengali fish curry already in the database
Gentle simmering keeps the fish tender
Third distinct regional fish preparation, broadening non-vegetarian variety

name: ZITLAS Prawn Cutlet Sandwich
description: Pan-fried prawn cutlets sandwiched in toasted bread — a distinct seafood-based cutlet-sandwich format from the fish cutlet sandwich already in the database.
ingredients: Ginger, green chilli, black pepper — 5 g
instructions: Finely chop the prawns and mix with onion, ginger, green chilli and black pepper.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until golden and firm on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Prawn gives a distinctly different texture (slightly springy) from the flaky fish cutlet already in the database
Fourth distinct non-vegetarian protein source represented across the database (egg, chicken, fish, mutton, and now prawn)
Portable sandwich format

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Khichu
description: A khichu made with finely chopped vegetables mixed into the rice-flour batter — a vegetable-forward variant of the Moong Dal Khichu and Sabudana Khichu in this batch.
instructions: Bring water to a boil with cumin seeds and ajwain.
Add finely chopped vegetables and simmer 2 minutes.
Slowly whisk in rice flour, stirring continuously to avoid lumps, until it thickens into a soft mass.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with warm oil, and eat with a spoon.
why_it_works: Vegetables cooked directly into the khichu base add fiber the plain or moong dal versions lack
Completes a set of three distinct khichu variants (moong dal, sabudana, vegetable) for different nutritional needs
One-pot, minimal cleanup

name: ZITLAS Egg Adai
description: Adai topped with a fried egg placed directly on top while cooking — a fourth distinct adai variant, adding a runny-yolk protein element not present in the plain, vegetable or paneer versions.
instructions: Soak rice and dals for at least 4 hours, grind coarsely with red chilli and ginger.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread into a coarse round.
Crack an egg directly onto the centre of the adai while the first side cooks, and let it set into the surface.
Drizzle oil around the edges, cover briefly to finish cooking the egg, and serve without flipping.
why_it_works: Egg cracked directly onto the adai surface (not mixed in or served alongside) is a distinct construction from the paneer-topped or vegetable-mixed versions
Runny yolk adds a different textural element from any other egg preparation in the database
High protein from both the multi-dal base and the egg

name: ZITLAS Prawn Biryani Bowl
description: Rice layered and dum-cooked with marinated prawns and biryani spices — a seafood biryani distinct from the vegetarian soya version already in the database.
instructions: Marinate the prawns in curd and biryani masala for 10-15 minutes.
Heat oil, fry sliced onion until golden and set aside half for garnish.
Layer partially-cooked rice with the marinated prawns and remaining fried onion in the cooker.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat (dum-style) for 10-12 minutes — prawns cook fast, so avoid overcooking.
Fluff gently and garnish with reserved onion.
why_it_works: Prawns cook far faster than chicken or mutton, so the dum time is shorter, a genuinely different technique consideration from a meat biryani
Seafood biryani variant distinct from the vegetarian soya version already in the database
Weekend-special feel with a quick-cooking protein

name: ZITLAS Lean Mutton Curry Rice Bowl
description: A light, home-style lean mutton curry served over rice — a curry-and-rice bowl format distinct from the stuffed keema paratha already using mutton in this batch.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until soft.
Add the mutton and garam masala, along with enough water to cover.
Pressure cook for 15-18 minutes until the mutton is tender.
Serve the curry over warm rice.
why_it_works: Curry-and-rice format is genuinely different from the stuffed paratha use of mutton earlier in this batch, giving a second distinct way to eat the same protein
Pressure cooking keeps this practical despite mutton's usually longer cooking time
Home-style, moderate spicing

name: ZITLAS Paneer Puttu Bowl
description: Steamed puttu crumbled and tossed with crumbled paneer — a dairy-protein-added puttu variant distinct from the vegetable or egg versions in this batch.
instructions: Prepare and steam puttu as usual with rice flour and grated coconut.
Warm the crumbled paneer briefly in a pan with a little oil and black pepper.
Crumble the steamed puttu into the pan and toss gently with the warmed paneer.
Serve warm in a bowl.
why_it_works: Paneer gives a creamier, richer protein addition than the egg or plain vegetable puttu variants
Completes a set of three distinct puttu bowl variants for different dietary preferences
Same steaming technique throughout

name: ZITLAS Mutton Seekh Kebab Bowl
description: Grilled lean mutton mince skewers served over a light salad — a distinct grilled-kebab format from the paratha or curry uses of mutton elsewhere in this batch.
instructions: Mix mutton mince with grated onion, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala, kneading well to bind.
Shape into small skewer-less kebabs (or thread onto skewers if available).
Grill in an oven or air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Serve over a bed of chopped cucumber and tomato.
why_it_works: Grilled kebab format is genuinely different from the stuffed paratha or curry preparations of mutton elsewhere in this batch, using no added oil beyond what's in the mince itself
Salad base keeps this lower carb than a bread-based mutton dish
Third distinct way to use lean mutton across the database

name: ZITLAS Egg Neer Dosa Bowl
description: Neer dosa torn into pieces and tossed with scrambled egg — a distinct combination format from serving neer dosa plain with a side curry.
instructions: Soak and grind rice into a very thin batter as for neer dosa; cook thin, soft dosas on a tawa.
Tear the cooked dosas into bite-sized pieces.
Heat oil, saute onion, then scramble in the beaten egg until just cooked.
Toss the torn neer dosa pieces with the scrambled egg.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Torn-and-tossed bowl format is genuinely different from serving neer dosa flat with a side curry
Egg addition raises the protein of a dish that's traditionally very light
Distinct from every other egg-and-grain combination in the database by the neer dosa's delicate texture

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chana Thalipeeth
description: A thalipeeth made with roasted chana (dalia) flour blended into the dough — a fifth distinct thalipeeth base, adding a nutty flavour and extra protein from roasted gram.
instructions: Mix sattu and bajra flour with onion, cumin seeds, ajwain and enough water to form a soft dough.
Pat directly onto a hot, lightly oiled tawa into a thin round.
Poke a few holes, drizzle oil, and cook covered until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Roasted gram flour gives notably more protein than the jowar-bajra-besan blend used in the standard thalipeeth
Nutty, toasted flavour distinct from the other thalipeeth variants in the database
Same reliable hand-patting technique

name: ZITLAS Baked Aloo Kachori
description: A whole wheat kachori filled with spiced mashed potato, baked — the third distinct filling for the baked-kachori format, alongside moong dal and paneer.
ingredients: Fennel seeds, coriander powder, red chilli — 6 g
instructions: Mix mashed potato with fennel seeds, coriander powder and red chilli for the filling.
Knead atta with a little oil and water into a firm dough.
Roll small discs, stuff with the potato filling, seal and flatten gently.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Serve with tamarind chutney.
why_it_works: Potato filling completes a set of three distinct kachori options (moong dal, paneer, potato) so users can pick by protein need or preference
Baked, not fried, keeping this meaningfully lighter than a traditional aloo kachori
Classic, widely-loved filling made healthier
